title: Automated sleuth playbook and telemetry needle detector
author: Marina Kozlov
description:
Motivation: on-call responders routinely surface the same investigative steps for a set of noisy but high-impact signals. This PR introduces two coordinated features: (1) a 'Sleuth Playbook' generator that emits graded runbooks based on a compact telemetry diff, and (2) a 'Telemetry Needle Detector' - a lightweight heuristic that surfaces unusual signal combinations (needles) which can drive playbook selection. The goal is to reduce cognitive load and time-to-action for first responders while preserving human-in-the-loop safety for mitigation steps.

Scope and user-facing behavior: the Sleuth Playbook is presented as a 3-tier action card (Inspect, Mitigate, Escalate) with suggested query snippets, required checks, and an estimated confidence score. The Needle Detector runs as a post-alert hook (configurable per-service) and annotates alerts with 'needle' tags and a short rationale. Playbook generation prioritizes non-destructive guidance; automatic mitigations are gated behind a staged 'canary execute' flow which requires both an explicit operator approval and two positive health checks.

Implementation highlights: a new micro-package incident-bot/sleuth/ contains the core heuristics, a compact fuzzy-diff algorithm for telemetry rollups, and a deterministic playbook templating engine. The detector runs in-process with the alert enrichment pipeline but offloads scoring to a bounded worker pool to protect alert throughput. A new runbook executor in slo-toolkit/runner adds a dry-run mode and a graded-execute API that opens a 30-minute operator window for canary runs. We also extended the Slack/Console cards to show the confidence band, needle provenance, and one-click dry-run.

Checklist:
- [x] Sleuth heuristics and templating engine with unit tests
- [x] Needle detector integration and sampling to avoid alert amplification
- [x] Dry-run and graded execution APIs with audit logs
- [x] UI card updates (Slack + Console) and telemetry for explainability
- [x] Safety gates (approval flow, health-check hooks) and policy config
- [x] End-to-end smoke tests and e2e harness updates

Backwards compatibility: the needle tag is an optional annotation and does not change existing alert routing. Playbook suggestions are additive and default to 'suggest-only' mode for the first 30 days in beta.

Operational notes: default sampling is 5% of alerts for needle detection on production; teams can opt-in to higher rates via project config. The worker pool uses a token bucket to avoid contention with high-throughput services. Rolling back: feature flags are behind feature/sleuth-playbook and can be disabled from the console or via the feature flags api.

Related tickets: ENG-2198 (playbook generator), ENG-2201 (runbook executor), SUP-4412 (customer request: faster triage for replication loop incidents).

review_comments: Omar Singh: This looks promising. Before we can allow graded-exec at scale we need a hard guardrail preventing auto-exec on services with external side-effects (billing, customer emails). Can you add a policy check?
Author (Marina Kozlov): Added a policy layer in graded_executor that checks service tags against an allowlist. Updated docs to show opt-in steps. See new tests in test_graded_executor_policy.py
Leah Thompson: E2E flake on the canary health-check timing observed in CI. Suggest increasing the test harness tolerance instead of changing prod timeouts.
Author: Increased harness tolerance and added a jitter cap; left prod health-check timeouts unchanged.
Diego Alvarez: Approve after minor nits (doc wording).
SRE WG (comment): Please monitor the needle-tag prevalence metric in the first week; default sampling is low but we want early telemetry.

release_notes: Adds Sleuth Playbook generation and a Telemetry Needle Detector that suggests graded runbooks and dry-run mitigations. Default suggest-only mode; auto-exec gated by policy and operator approval. Configurable sampling; see docs/oncall/sleuth_playbooks.md for rollout steps and opt-in instructions.
